extracted.intended_audience: CIA management, procurement/logistics offices, and OFPP/federal procurement officials
extracted.subtask_description: A CIA comment memorandum on the proposed revisions to OMB Circular A-76 outlining the Agency actions required by the draft circular and explaining why CIA cannot fully comply because of the need to protect intelligence sources and methods. The document lists required inventories, review schedules, disclosure obligations, and recommends formally advising OFPP of CIA's limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compile a complete inventory of all commercial and industrial activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediately compile a complete inventory of all commercial and industrial activities (those that provide a product or service that could be obtained from the private sector), complete with a description of each activity, the Government's capital investment, annual cost of operation, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed A-76 requires an immediate, comprehensive listing including descriptive and financial data for each activity; this is presented as a mandatory deliverable to OFPP and a basis for review. Security-classified activities present problems for full disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare and furnish a detailed schedule for review of activities and contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediately prepare and furnish a detailed schedule for the review of each commercial or industrial activity and each contract in excess of $100,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The schedule must cover every listed activity and every contract above the $100,000 threshold; the review's purpose is to determine whether continued operation is consistent with A-76 requirements. The memorandum emphasizes the immediacy of this obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose inventory and review information to OFPP and the private sector
rubrics_metrics.description: Make all or substantially all of the above information available to OFPP and the private sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The draft circular expects agencies to provide the compiled inventory and review schedules to OFPP and private-sector entities. The CIA letter notes that full disclosure—much of which is classified—would make implementation impossible for CIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine if continued operation is consistent with A-76 requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Review each activity and contract to determine if continued Government operation is consistent with A-76 requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This substantive determination is the central evaluative step of the review process mandated by the proposed circular and follows from the inventory and scheduled reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of compliance (immediate implementation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed revisions require immediate compilation of inventories and immediate preparation/furnishing of review schedules and related data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memorandum repeatedly stresses 'immediately' for the inventory and schedules, indicating that OFPP expects prompt/aggressive implementation rather than phased or delayed action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect intelligence sources and methods (statutory responsibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: The overriding factor preventing full CIA compliance is the DCI's statutory responsibility to protect intelligence sources and methods—in its many manifestations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory duty may preclude disclosure or actions required by A-76; the memorandum frames protection of classified sources/methods as a non-negotiable constraint that can supersede the circular's written requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with intent of A-76 while recognizing written requirements may be infeasible
rubrics_metrics.description: While we feel we comply with the intent of the Circular, we cannot comply with the written words and still satisfy the DCI's statutory responsibility to protect intelligence sources and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommended approach is to demonstrate compliance with the Circular's intent (e.g., reliance on private sector where appropriate) but to assert inability to meet specific written disclosure/processing requirements that would reveal classified information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate degree of reliance on the private sector and ability to expand support
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide sufficient information to allow OFPP to appreciate the uniqueness of CIA activities: demonstrate the degree to which CIA relies on the private sector and the agency's ability to expand such support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quantitative and descriptive evidence (e.g., 'over 25 percent of our 1978 appropriation will be spent in the private sector', 'Approximately 70 percent of our active contracts ... are classified') to show reliance while clarifying security constraints on disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate comments internally before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate and prepare comments/letter in consultation with relevant internal offices (Offices of Logistics, General Counsel, and the DDS&T).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The attached letter had been 'fully coordinated' with those offices; internal coordination is presented as necessary prior to formal submission to OFPP to ensure legal, logistical, and technical consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formally advise OFPP of unique mission constraints and inability to comply
rubrics_metrics.description: Formally advise OFPP that, because of the unique nature of CIA activities, CIA cannot comply with the provisions of the proposed Circular A-76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memorandum recommends forwarding a signed letter (via the CIA Budget Examiner) to the Administrator, OFPP, to put on the record CIA's position—that it complies with the Circular's intent but cannot meet written disclosure/implementation requirements without violating statutory responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to OFPP comment deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide comments on the proposed changes by the OFPP-requested deadline (in this document, 23 October 1978).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memorandum notes OFPP's deadline and treats timely response as a procedural requirement when submitting formal comments to the policy office.
